question: The new /health route is unauthenticated and reachable from anything on the local network — why wasn't it at least rate-limited?
reference_answer: Rate limiting was rejected because it would need per-caller state that nothing in the codebase currently tracks, and /health costs no more to serve than the already-unlimited /hello route, so limiting only the new route would add no real protection.

gold.quote: Needs per-caller state in a file that has none, and `/health` is no cheaper to serve than `/hello`, which is already unlimited.

question: Why did the team reject reading package.json fresh on every incoming request instead of once at startup?
reference_answer: Reading the manifest per request was rejected because it introduces per-request file I/O and a per-request failure path to serve a value that only changes when the process restarts anyway.

gold.heading_path: 0001: Read the version once at module load with require('../package.json') > Alternatives
gold.quote: Introduces per-request file I/O and a per-request failure path (a 500 or a crash) to serve a value that only changes on restart anyway (intent Outcome 4).
